lines.en: The trip to Yasu’s church feels a little different in the summer.
Along with the cold comes a terrifying silence that unsettles my stomach with every sacrilegious step toward the sanctuary.
But the heat of this new season masks those sounds with a soundtrack of its own.

The silence has died. And in its place rests a barrage of endless insectual (A made up word not to be confused with “incestual” that pertains to the quality of being a [[or being created by an] insect) melodies-
The creatures sing to me as if I am one of them.
They sing to me as if to welcome me home.
And in turn, I bend my legs backward and turn them into makeshift coils, springing into the sky like the world’s largest camel cricket and coming closer to the moon than necessary.
Its light reminds me of who I am and where I’ve been.
Its light reminds me of why I’m here and what I am to do next.
And so I take my coiled legs and unfurl them into the shapes I have grown familiar with.
Triangle. Circle. Triangle.
None of which you understand.
But to me, it makes perfect sense.
To me, this all makes perfect sense.
If it didn’t, I wouldn’t find myself amidst this INSECTUAL chorus with my mind half drowned in a bathtub full of honey while the rest figures out a way to float atop it.
I come close enough to the sky that I can smell the clouds, but the putrid stench of the cumulocirrus outlines of all of the things I have lost is enough to bring me back to the ground.
It is enough to make me seek salvation in a way much different than I am meant to.
It is enough to have me curl my fingers around the handle of the door to a building in a city that houses a girl who I will one day fill with my light.
It is enough to remind me that I have always hated the summer.
And that I will continue to hate it until the day I die once more.

When I step inside, I am greeted by the sight of the girl I came to see electing to spend time with a colony of inanimate rabbits rather than someone actually capable of listening to her perpetual psychobabble.
Perhaps it is because they are incapable of running away like the rest of us do.
Or perhaps it is because somewhere, buried beneath all of the fluff and feathers or whatever it is they stuff inside of creatures like them is something that can hear.
Perhaps they are creatures who can feel.
I mean, we’re all stuffed with something, aren’t we?
How is what’s inside of us any better when we’re the ones who will expire while they live on forever?
Granted, this is all just hopeful conjecture bent into shapes that will make the girl I came to see look less damaged under the glow of the church lights.
Triangle. Circle. Triangle.
I can hear a god forming beneath the stone floor.
: What’s wrong, Penemue?
: You’ve barely touched your eggs.
: If you don’t clear your plate, you won’t be able to come to the white room with us.
: That would be a terrible shame, don’t you agree?
: And you, Wormwood. You’ve had four whole glasses of tea today. Don’t you think that may be a little much?
: If you drink any more, you’re certain to get a tummy ache. And I’m afraid I am fresh out of dried papaya to help fix you.
: Is that so? You brought your own?
: My, since when are you so responsible?
: Penemue could learn a thing or two from you.
I think about calling out to Yasu and putting an end to whatever weird charade this is but, at the same time, I can’t help but be fascinated by the way she speaks to them.
It’s different than the way she communicates with people- the way she communicates with me.
And, for lack of a better term (And I don’t mean to sound insulting), it makes her feel...human.
Much like the way her sudden interest in solo karaoke did at the Christmas party but, this time around, things actually seem to be a little more depressing.
Though, that may just be because Touka isn’t here to dampen her infinite loneliness this time and that, instead, Yasu has taken to quelling that issue in a new way. One that-
: How long are you going to stand there for, Sensei?
: Haven’t you come to join the tea party?
: ...I didn’t realize you knew I was here.
: The cathedral doors are rather loud. And Wormwood here hates the sound of insects that floods the room each time the doors are opened.
: Please, sit down with us. The festivities are just getting started...and they have been looking forward to meeting you.
: The...stuffed animals have been looking forward to meeting me?
: Is that what you see?
: Well...that’s what they are. So, yes.
: Also, what festivities? Is there actually some kind of reason for this...weird cathedral tea party thing?
: There is!
: It is our celebration of summer!
: A new coming of our humble god is upon us. And we have gathered here today to welcome Him and drink in His love!
: This tea was brewed with water fresh from the basement ceiling and leaves gathered from the alley behind the cathedral.
: To become closer to God, we must partake in the pieces of Him. And in doing so, we will be granted safety, serenity, and forgiveness for the sins we have committed but have yet to realize.
: You gathered leaves from the alley and turned them into tea?
: Not just any tea, Sensei. Tea that brings us closer to Him. Don’t you want to try?
: Wormwood has already had four cups and he is very picky when it comes to fluids. I’m sure you’ll love it as well.
: I’m good, Yasu. Thanks.
: At the very least, will you sit with us and partake in the rest of the celebration?
: Their feelings will be very hurt if you leave after coming all this way.
: Sure. But...just to reiterate, I am not drinking your weird ceiling water tea.
I move to the opposite side of the table and pull out the only chair not occupied by the lifeless body of a rabbit.
I wonder if this seat being empty means that Yasu anticipated me coming here and, if so...why?
It’s not like I haven’t come here of my own volition in the past, but I’m far from being considered a regular at this point and...there was really no reason for her to believe I would show up.
: Yasu.
: Yes?
: You weren’t expecting me, were you?
: Of course I was.
: But...why?
: Because even if it is not yet apparent to you, your heart beats in tune with His.
: You were always going to wind up here for the celebration whether or not you knew it.
: Deep down inside, you love the summer. The same way we do.
: You mean you and the rabbits?
: I suppose, if that is what makes this easier for you to understand.
: I don’t think anything is going to make this easier to understand.
: You are free to ask any questions you may have.
: Penemue may not be in the brightest of moods today, but he is very knowledgeable when it comes to our reasons to be.
: And Wormwood is a font of information when it comes to the history of our God.
: There’s also Muriel...and Yomiel...and Zachariel...and many others hidden in the background who would be more than happy to hold your hand as you embark on your journey closer to us, Sensei.
: Again, I’m good. I’m just...here to hang out with you, really.
: Hang out?
: Yeah. You know...spend time together. As like, friends. Or...whatever we are.
: Heheh...
: We are not friends, Sensei.
: You know, it really hurts when you, of all people, are the one saying that.
: That isn’t to say that I don’t want to be your friend. I would love that.
: But I am entirely undeserving.
: Besides...there’s something much more important that we have to do. Something that transcends the relationship of even lovers, let alone friends.
: Right. Fill the world with light or whatever.
: If only it were that simple.
: You see, one of my favorite things about summer is that His voice becomes much clearer.
: Which means that my purpose becomes much clearer in turn.
: And that purpose is?
: Yasu?
: I’m sorry...
: He doesn’t want me to tell you.
: Okay, well...this is the last time I come to one of your tea parties.
: This is the last party we’ll be having for quite some time. And I’m sure you’ll have changed your mind by the time the next one comes around.
: That is how He has envisioned it.
: That is where things will go from here.
: And if they don’t?
: Sensei, you don’t understand.
: That’s just not possible.
: Yasu-
: I am the one who hears the call! I am the one who witnesses His future for Him!
: Who plays it back like the broken record this life is!
: He knows what will happen because it has happened before!
: It will happen again!
: Summer has come, Sensei!
: He sleeps no longer!
: Enlighten him, Wormwood!
: Yasu, I’m not going to talk to-
: To build a wall or break one down;\nIt depends on what you want.
: To see a world outside of mirrors;\nOr bathe in holy fonts.
: We all have things that we must do;\nYou, too, must fill your role.
: For if you don’t, we all will fall;\nFurther down the rabbit hole.
: Feel the caress of the wind as it slips in through the sleeves of your shirt! This is Him!
: The undeniable solemnity you feel when gazing up at your ceiling! The one that does not leak! This is Him!
: The shaking of the trees! The creaking of the floorboards! It is all Him!
: He is all around us!
: He is in me!
: I can feel him bursting out like a possessed holy embryo with fingernails growing at twenty times the rate of that of a normal human being!
: He claws His way out!
: Can you see Him?
: He wants to emerge!
: CAN YOU SEE HIM?!
: Don’t answer His questions with responses you know not to be true.
: Not after all He has done for you.
: See...that’s just the thing.
: He has done nothing for me.
: No god has ever done anything for me. They’re all just stories that people latch onto so they can have something to look forward to when they die.
: Or...something they force themselves to believe in so they can have some sort of code to live by.
: But none of them are real. Yours included.
: But hey, if you want to waste away your days talking to stuffed animals instead of people, that’s fine. I’ve got no right to tell you how to live your life.
: But you should stop trying to make me live mine the way you do by shoving these stories down my throat every time I come here.
: But, Sensei-
: You wouldn’t come here at all if you didn’t long for the sensation of something stuck inside of your throat.
: What difference does it make if it is the word of the lord or the tongue of the one He brought back?
: The...what?
: Heheh...hahahahahahHH!H!H!H!HAHAHAHAHuiywegfdiusdhfiuodghfuohasdifougdhsa!!
: YOU KNOW IT TO BE TRUE! WHICH IS WHY YOUR DENIAL NOW IS STRONGER THAN EVER BEFORE!
: YOU HAVE NOT JUST SEEN HIM AT THIS POINT!
: YOU HAVE BEEN TOUCHED BY HIM!
: I CAN SMELL HIS SCENT ALL OVER YOU! THE ONE TRUE APHRODISIAC! CLINGING TO THE FABRIC OF YOUR COAT AND MAKING ME FEEL WAYS I HAVE SELDOM FELT BEFORE!
: COME TO ME! COME TO ME IN YOUR PUREST FORM!
: COME TO ME BEFORE ALL OF MY FRIENDS IN THE HOUSE OF MY FATHER AND RUB HIS SCENT ON ME!
: RUB HIS SCENT ON ME!
: RUB HIS SCENT ON-
: NGH!
Yasu winds up screaming at me so loudly that she gives herself a headache.
Which, at this point in time, I can safely say is probably the best thing that has happened to me today.
Or, at least it would be if I wasn’t actually worried about her health right now as it seems this might actually be kind of serious.
: Uhh...religious stuff aside, are you okay? Because it looks like-
: I am fine! This is nothing in the face of all He has felt!
: Please help yourself to some of Penemue’s eggs, Sensei! Partake in the bountiful feast He has provided us! One that transcends time itself!
: Reserve your space in the white room! There is nowhere else that can protect us from-
: AAAAHHH! IT HURTS!
: IT HURTS, IT HURTS, IT HURTS!
: It doesn’t hurt at all!
: It feels better than anything I’ve ever felt before!
: Come to me!
: Come! Come! Come!
: A LIE, A LIE, ALIGN!;\nTHE STARS BENEATH THE SKY!
: CHERISH THOSE WHO LOVE THEM AND RELINQUISH YOUR CONTROL!
: FEEL HIS GIFTS! RETURN HIS LOVE!
: CLIMB FURTHER DOWN THE RABBIT HOLE!
: Okay. It’s time we get you back to-
: Yasu?
When I turn back around, it’s like she was never here at all.
Yasu, the rabbits, and all of the tea had vanished into thin air.
All that was left was a table, some chairs, and a plate full of eggs.
I chalked it up to another delusion and headed home.
The sound of insects along the way was louder than ever before.
When I got into bed that night, it felt as if my legs had been broken.
Or, at the very least, bent backwards.
Yasu’s affection has increased to [yasu_love]!
